**Yes—the reproduced minimum-gap blocker is resolved by candidate0039. I found no new carry or phase regression in the inspected code and focused reruns.**

- [m_lattice.lua:523](<mosaic-worktree>/lib/clock/m_lattice.lua:523) clamps before the unchanged rounding/carry calculation. [m_clock.lua:623](<mosaic-worktree>/lib/clock/m_clock.lua:623) advances startup once; `begin_cycle()` selects the next division before consuming carry.
- I reran [arp_minimum_gap_contract.lua:19](<mosaic-worktree>/tests/behaviour/arp_minimum_gap_contract.lua:19): negative50 gives `1,4,5,6`, positive50 gives `4,5,6,7`; both startup regressions pass. Removing only the clamp **in memory** reproduces `1,4,6` and fails the assertion.

- Both native artifacts match the current lattice hash; manifest artifact hashes verify. Recorded MIDI confirms onsets `0,1,4,5,6` and `0,4,5,6,7`, with five releases each. The [native oracle:1204](<mosaic-worktree>/tests/behaviour/cases.py:1204) checks exact onsets/MIDI and independently declared parent cycles with the stated one-pulse release bound.
- The five corrected integration schedules agree with the [recorded recurrence](<mosaic-worktree>/docs/testing/decisions.md:94); their per-pulse empty-queue assertions reject extra MIDI.

**One concrete test-maintenance issue:** [conditional_realign_contract.lua:25](<mosaic-worktree>/tests/behaviour/conditional_realign_contract.lua:25) lacks the new `chord_timing` include and fails before testing behavior. Supplying that include in memory makes all 64 cases pass; update the fixture. This is not evidence of a scheduler regression.

**CONFIDENCE: High for this blocker.** I did not independently rerun all 474 units or establish final native/real-time acceptance; candidate0038 and full-release completion remain outside this clearance.
